content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce is a home recipe where cooked noodles are coated with a smooth sauce made from cream, cheese, garlic and spices. The dish is quick to prepare, has a mild creamy flavor and works well for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream sauce is often made with 20 % cream and grated Parmesan, giving it a distinctive aroma.
In Italy pasta is traditionally served "al dente", slightly firm in the center, so the sauce adheres better.
Making the sauce at home allows better control of taste and salt content compared to store‑bought packets.
Variations may include mushrooms, ham or spinach for a richer flavor profile.
The cream used in the sauce is rich in fatty acids, which, in moderation, contribute to satiety.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cream and cheese in the sauce provide calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: Pasta supplies complex carbohydrates while the cream sauce adds fats, making the meal calorie‑rich and satisfying.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Enriched cream can be a source of vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Supports nervous system
items.content: B‑vitamins present in pasta help maintain normal nervous system function.

items.title: Enhances flavor perception
items.content: Fats in the cream sauce amplify aromas and taste, making the dish more enjoyable.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The cream sauce is rich in fat, so the dish can be high‑calorie and may not suit strict diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream and cheese may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy should avoid the cream sauce.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Adding a lot of cheese or using a prepared sauce can raise the salt content, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta until al dente. In a separate pan heat the cream, add grated Parmesan, minced garlic, salt and pepper, and stir until the sauce is smooth. Drain the pasta, combine it with the sauce and heat for 1‑2 minutes so the noodles are fully coated.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Pasta is best served immediately, but can be kept in the fridge for up to 2 days, reheating with a splash of cream or water.
